newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish parliament snubs call for referendum choice.
newsitem.headline: Polish parliament snubs call for referendum choice.

text.p: Poland's right-wing ROP movement was rebuffed on Monday after it brought hundreds of thousands of signatures to parliament calling for a clearer choice in this month's constitutional referendum.
Members of the Reconstruction of Poland movement (ROP) staged a protest outside the parliament building after being told the petition would not be considered.
"This is our protest against lower house speaker Jozef Zych who said that reviewing our petition was impossible," PAP news agency quoted ROP spokesman Andrzej Kierylo as saying.

He said ROP had 520,000 signatures on a petition to give voters a choice between two constitutions in the May 25 vote, rather than asking them to accept or reject a draft constitution passed on April 2 by the left-dominated parliament.
ROP wants voters to be allowed the chance to back a version drawn up by the right-leaning Solidarity movement.

Earlier on Monday, Solidarity leader Marian Krzaklewski praised ROP's petition as a symbolic gesture which could encourage more people to reject the parliamentary draft, but said he doubted the referendum could be altered just two weeks before the vote.
Poland has been functioning under an interim constitution since 1992. If voted in, the new constitution, will replace a 1952 document made redundant after the 1989 fall of communism.
